text:
jamie: quick note — ran a thin-slab warmup + post-bind sweep on paged-KV for the 8k seq workload. OOMs dropped from 4/day -> 0 in canary, but p50 token latency went up ~12ms. looks like allocation hotpath changed cache locality. :thinking:
ravi: can you paste the profiler / flamegraph? p50 jump could be extra memcpy or sync in the allocator path. :eyes:
jamie: pasted sampling trace below (top-down, truncated):
```
flamegraph: paged_kv_alloc -> slab_acquire -> gpu_lock_wait (30%) -> memcpy_h2d (18%) -> kernel_select (12%)
also noticed small spikes in cudaMemcpy when slab rebinds happened
```
sofia: interesting — if warmup pre-allocs thin slabs we prevent OOM but might be increasing cold misses for the attention kernel. are we forcing kernel fallback or changing kernel_choice_policy?
jamie: no explicit kernel change. kernel selection logs say same FlashAttn-v2 chosen, but there are more short-lived allocations before request batching completes. my hypothesis: extra H2D due to slab rebinds and KV page table repairs.
ciara: could be fragmentation plus deferred free list merge. did you try a quick patch to merge freed thin slabs synchronously?
jamie: yes. synchronous merge reduced memcpy spikes but increased CPU stall time and made p50 worse (~18ms). so tradeoff.
alex: what about reordering free-list to LIFO for thin slabs only (better cache reuse) instead of FIFO? that should reduce H2D churn w/o global sync.
jamie: tried LIFO in canary for 2 hours — p50 improved back ~6ms (so net +6ms vs baseline) and OOMs stayed at 0. promising.
sofia: any telemetry on batch sizes? if batching heuristic shrank batches due to mem pressure we could be paying extra kernel overheads.
jamie: batching histograms: before warmup median batch_size=12, after warmup median=9, with more 1-3 small batches. warmup seems to cause earlier KV allocation making scheduler cut batches.
ravi: that suggests scheduler/backpressure signal is seeing more memory transient and throttling. can we add a short grace window after warmup where scheduler waits to accumulate tokens (100ms)?
jamie: I added `batch_accum_grace_ms=120` in canary. results: p50 dropped to +3ms vs baseline, p99 unchanged, and throughput recovered ~98% of baseline.
perf-bot: CI bench summary for canary commit 5f3a2: 8k_seq throughput -1.6%, p50 +3.1ms, OOMs 0/24h. perf regression alert: minor p50 increase flagged but under debug. link: https://ci.internal/bench/5f3a2
ciara: also worth checking block-table rebuild cost. if we rebuild slab metadata on every page-in, that's extra work. can we incrementally repair metadata instead?
jamie: looking at code — `block_table::repair()` does full scan on page-in currently. I sketched incremental repair that only touches affected buckets.
sofia: incremental repair + LIFO thin-slab + batch_accum_grace seems like the combo to try. also add metric for `page_in_repaired_buckets` so we can detect large repairs.
jiamie: agreed. I'll open a PR with three patches: LIFO free-list, incremental repair, batch grace (config flag). will include perf tests and flamegraphs.
alex: note to validate with fused-attn kernel too — latency sensitivity differs. test both FlashAttn-v2 and fused-attn in canary matrix.
jamie: good call. will run matrix.
deploy-bot: canary deployment 5f3a2 -> eng-runtime-canary started (region: us-west-2).
ravi: assigned to jamie to follow up on PR and to add the `page_in_repaired_buckets` metric. please paste the PR link here when ready.
jiamie: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4221 — contains tests, perf runs, and rollback plan. tagging @sofia @ciara for review.
sofia: reviewing now. quick comment: add a gauge for `thin_slab_free_list_len` so we can monitor pretenure health.
jamie: ack. will add.
ciara: follow-up action: add a microbenchmark that simulates heavy page-in patterns at 8k seq and runs kernel-choice toggles so we can reproduce locally. I'll sketch one today.
jamie: thanks — next update by EOD with initial perf numbers from the matrix. :thumbsup:
